column1: # TITLE: Transcriptomic analysis of PD-L1 positive and negative hot lung adenocarcinomas identifies a different molecular immunogenic landscape
# SUMMARY: Lung cancer is a major global health problem
column2: as it is the leading cause of cancer- related deaths worldwide. Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
column4: is a heterogeneous disease with adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma being the predominant subtypes. Immune-inhibiting interaction of Programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) with programmed cell death-protein 1 (PD-1) causes checkpoint mediated immune evasion and is
column6: an important therapeutic target in cancer. In NSCLC
column7: improved understanding of PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint blockade-responsive biology is warranted. We aimed to identify the landscape of immune cell infiltration in primary lung adeno- carcinoma (LUAD) in the context of tumor PD-L1 expression and the extent of immune infiltration (“hot” vs. “cold” phenotype). Therefore
column8: the study comprises LUAD cases (n=138) with “hot” and “cold” tumor immune phenotype and positive and negative tumor PD-L1 expression
column9: respectively. Tumor samples were immunohistochemically analyzed for expression of PD-L1
column10: CD4 and CD8 and further analyzed on transcriptomic level by Nanostring nCouter Pan Cancer Immune Profiling Panel. We detected significantly differentially expressed genes associated with PD-L1 positive and “hot” versus PD-L1 negative and “cold” phenotype. The presented study illustrates novel aspects of PD-L1 regulation
column12: as well as relevance for immunotherapy response stratification.
